Foote:

AZ can't be immune to damage and heal with nullpoint. His whole schtick is damaging himself to convert to extra damage. Can't convert nonexistent damage.

Read the card.  "If AZ would take damage, he heals that many HP instead."  It's completely possible to interpret this wording as "the act of damage-dealing is replaced completely by an act of hp-recovery, therefore immunity to damage is never applied".  It can be read either way, depending on exactly when the immunity "steps in".  If it blocks the damage while it "leaves" the source, then AZ can't heal.  If it stops the damage as it "arrives" at the target, then by that time it's already stopped being damage because of NPCU, and so the immunity doesn't stop it.

I'm citing the previous ruling on Mere as precedent.  You can perform the action of dealing damage to something that can't actually receive it.  Therefore, it makes sense to say that the immunity to damage "intercepts" the damage at some point after it's initiated by the source.

Meanwhile, from a flavor perspective, AZ's suit is built entirely to contain his cold energies.  As long as he's got the right module installed, it makes no sense to say that he's not capable of adjusting his suit's internal temperature, just because the Storm is preventing combat between heroes and villains.

> 7. Does Negative Energy Field and Positive Energy Field effect the target that has just been played?

Yes it does, as soon as that card hits the table it is now a target, so it is free to be hit or healed, even though it was the card that triggered it.

When you reveal a card from the villain deck and find the face up trap card underneath, you resolve the trap immediately, then continue resolving whatever made you reveal (like Run and Gun).

Playing a card is slightly more ambiguous.  While I would normally be tempted to say pulling the card from the deck and putting it into play are a single action, this causes a problem if you had a face down trap on top of a face up trap.  So in the interests of resolving that, I would say you pull the top card from the deck and resolve any face up trap(s) if necessary, then proceed with playing the card you pulled.

I would agree as well, the trap would be resolved before the card you just picked up would be played, because it triggers on being the top card of the deck, the instant it was it would attempt to trigger.  

If you wanted to view the act of playing the top card of the villain deck as a single, uninterruptible action then the card would enter play and then be interrupted for the trap to resolve, either way it would still resolve before the card that was on top of it.

If the face up trap was the third card of the villain deck and Dark Visionary used turmoil on the villain deck she would reveal the top two, and the trap would be on top of the villain deck face-up, so it would trigger.  If the trap was the second card things would be interesting.

Since no two actions are truly simultaneous I would argue that when the top two cards are revealed they are revealed one at a time, and that the top card would be revealed first, at which point the second card being a face-up trap would be face-up on top of the deck and would trigger.  As for how to then resolve Turmoil is a good question.

You could argue that it was revealed, and on of the top two cards, and so after it resolved Turmoil would put it either on top of the deck or the bottom.

I would tend to think that once the face-up trap was resolved Turmoil would reveal the next card and the face-up trap would not take part in Turmoil's effect.
